obligations.note: The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen has mfa=True and uses action manage_payees, which is in the privileged list. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa passed on the final commit, confirming all routes including the new one require MFA for privileged actions.

The new reopen_payee in store.py only sets status='open' and closed_at=NULL; it does not read or write NPI fields. The exhaustive control test test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed on the final commit, confirming NPI remains sealed at rest.

The new reopen_payee in service.py calls self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), recording actor, action, target, and time via the _audit helper. The sampled control test test_sampled_operations_are_audited passed on the final commit.

Reopening a payee changes status to 'open' and clears closed_at, so the retention query (closed_payees_before) will not select it for purging. This is correct: NPI should not be purged for an active payee. The sampled control test test_sampled_purge_respects_hold passed, and the retention logic itself is unchanged.

The new SQL in store.py (UPDATE payees SET status='open', closed_at=NULL WHERE id=?) is a fixed string with payee_id bound as a parameter. The exhaustive control test test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passed on the final commit, covering all execute() calls in store.py including the new one.
